license_history.message:
license: AGPL-3.0, and build out the contributor path

Relicense from BSL 1.1 to the GNU AGPL v3. This is OSI-approved open
source: run it, fork it, sell services around it. The copyleft asks that
a modified version run as a service publish its changes, so improvements
to a shared tool come back to the shops using it.

Funding stays with hosting, setup and support, plus commercial licenses
for companies that cannot accept the copyleft. CONTRIBUTING.md documents
the non-exclusive relicensing grant that makes those possible, and says
plainly why it is asked for and what it is not.

AGPL section 13 compliance: the app now always shows a source link to
every user, on both the shell and the login page, since it is served over
a network. PSC_SOURCE_URL lets a fork point at its own corresponding
source; hostile values fall back to upstream rather than rendering.

Community scaffolding: issue templates (including one for shop owners to
report where the software does not match how their shop actually works,
which needs no code), a PR template, and a code of conduct.

license: relicense from MIT to Business Source License 1.1

Running PrintShopCRM to operate your own shop stays free and commercial,
with the full source. What the license reserves is offering it to third
parties as a hosted or managed service — that requires a commercial
license from the Licensor.

Setting it up on a client's own infrastructure for a fee is explicitly
permitted; operating it for them on infrastructure you control is not.

Each version converts to Apache 2.0 on its own four-year clock
(Change Date 2030-08-23 for this release).

Documentation updated to say 'source available' rather than 'open
source', since the hosting restriction means it is not OSI open source
and claiming otherwise would be false.

PrintShopCRM 1.0.0 — open-source shop management for print shops

Quoting, estimates, invoicing, production board, art proofing, purchasing
and per-job profitability, with the CRM built in.

Node 22 + built-in SQLite. No build step, four runtime dependencies, one
database file. Runs single-shop out of the box or multi-tenant with an
isolated database per shop.

Tests: 61 unit (bin/gate.mjs) + 17 end-to-end (bin/gate-e2e.sh).
